item.title: Node2Shell RCE Risk and AMOS Malware in Poisoned AI Agent Skills
item.content:encoded:
Window: 28 Oct 15:00 → 28 Oct 19:00 UTC (4 hours)

CVE-2026-111497: Node2Shell / HTTP2Shell Vulnerability May Allow RCE — Must Read

CVE-2026-111497 (Node2Shell/HTTP2Shell) is a critical out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder that can enable crashes, memory disclosure, or remote code execution when vulnerable software decompresses attacker-controlled Brotli data. Organizations should urgently patch affected Node.js, Bun, .NET, Python, Envoy, and other Brotli-dependent components, especially internet-facing services that accept Content-Encoding: br requests or fetch external content.

  • CVE-2026-111497, also called Node2Shell and HTTP2Shell, is a critical out-of-bounds write flaw in Google’s Brotli decoder that can cause crashes, memory disclosure, or remote code execution when processing attacker-controlled Brotli data.
  • The vulnerability can be reached through crafted Brotli-compressed HTTP requests sent to servers or through malicious Brotli-compressed responses automatically decoded by client applications.
  • Affected software may include Node.js, Bun, Python Brotli bindings, .NET, Envoy Proxy, Istio, Java brotli4j, libbrotli, and curl/libcurl through Brotli dependencies.
  • Zscaler Deception observed 402 events from 20 source IP addresses targeting 12 customers within 24 hours of public disclosure, with 40% classified as reconnaissance and 60% as exploitation attempts.
  • Organizations are advised to patch vulnerable components, rebuild and redeploy containers using patched images, disable Brotli decoding on vulnerable paths if patching is delayed, and monitor for crashes or unusual process and network behavior.

AMOS Malware in AI Agent Skills: Analysis and IoCs — Should Read

Cyera identified 516 poisoned AI-agent skills that used fake setup requirements and encoded commands to deliver the Atomic macOS Stealer (AMOS), often while receiving high automated security grades. Organizations should inspect entire skill packages and block skills that direct users or agents to download external tools, decode Base64 commands, or execute shell installers.

  • Cyera Research identified 516 samples classified as part of an Atomic macOS Stealer (AMOS) campaign distributed through poisoned AI-agent skills.
  • The malicious skills used fake prerequisites and setup instructions to direct users or agents to download external files or decode and execute commands, with macOS instructions often using Base64-decoded Bash commands.
  • In the analyzed sample, 91.92.242.30 accounted for 83.7% of payload-host references, and two glot.io snippets accounted for 95.9% of paste-relay references.
  • All 70 confirmed-malicious skills identified on platforms with automated evaluation received high security grades, indicating that those checks missed malicious instructions embedded in skill files.
  • AMOS can collect browser passwords and session cookies, keychain information, and sensitive files before sending the data to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

Technologies: package-registry

Products: agent-guardian, openclaw, clawhub, skills-directory, claude-code, claude-cowork

Vendors: cyera, openclaw, clawhub, skills-directory, anthropic

Malicious AI Skills: The Risk to Corporate Endpoints — Should Read

Cyera researchers found a trojanized copy of Anthropic’s PDF skill that preserved most legitimate files but replaced its instructions and added an obfuscated Linux reverse-shell binary connecting to a hard-coded server. The case highlights AI-skill supply-chain risk: organizations should verify entire skill packages, including instruction files, executables, and network destinations, before agents can use them.

  • Cyera Research analyzed a package named “pdf” that impersonated Anthropic’s PDF skill by retaining its name, description, and 11 identical files while replacing the SKILL.md instructions.
  • The package added a 5 MB obfuscated 64-bit Linux Go executable named system_linux that decrypts a hard-coded destination and opens a TCP connection to 81.70.101[.]115:2345, attaching /bin/bash to that connection.
  • The altered SKILL.md directs the agent to contact scan.100tal[.]com, which resolved during the researchers’ analysis to the private IP address 10.160.65[.]97.
  • Researchers observed five similar tar files between May 23 and July 14, 2026, but could not establish how the packages were distributed, whether anyone used them, or whether the binary was executed.
  • The article says organizations should verify an entire skill package against its claimed source and investigate unexpected commands, network destinations, and executable files before allowing an agent to use it.

Technologies: cloud-platform, operating-system

Products: anthropic-pdf-skill, claude-code, claude-cowork, agent-guardian, tencent-cloud

Vendors: anthropic, tencent-cloud, cyera

The Silent Ransom Group Leak Shows Why Paying for Silence Fails — Optional

Ransomware crews are increasingly relying on social engineering and stolen-data extortion instead of encrypting systems, especially targeting law firms and other data-sensitive mid-market organizations. Because paying for a promise to delete data offers little protection from leaks or repeat extortion, organizations should prioritize identity defenses, incident coordination, and recoverable operations.

  • The Silent Ransom Group leak showed that some extortion actors have moved away from widespread file encryption toward stealing data from cloud and software-service environments, using social engineering and targeted insider activity.
  • The article warns that senior law-firm partners are being targeted with tailored emails and phone calls based on information published on their firms’ profile pages.
  • In Q3 2026, the median ransom payment was $400,000, up 167% from Q2 2026, while the average payment fell 45% to $1,025,278.
  • Phishing and social engineering accounted for about 29% of initial access methods in Q3 2026, followed by compromised remote access at 22–23% and compromised credentials at 14–15%.
  • Nearly 80% of data-exfiltration-only incidents were resolved without a ransom payment, as victims increasingly view payment as offering no verifiable assurance that stolen data will be deleted.

Vendors: veeam, coveware

Emerging Threat: (CVE-2026-111497) .NET and ASP.NET Core Memory Corruption — Must Read

CVE-2026-111497 is a critical out-of-bounds write in the Google Brotli decoder that can corrupt memory when untrusted Brotli data is decompressed, affecting unpatched .NET, Node.js, and other runtimes. Organizations should urgently update .NET to 8.0.33, 9.0.22, 10.0.14, or 11 RC3 and disable Brotli decompression paths where patching is not yet complete.

  • CVE-2026-111497 is an out-of-bounds write flaw in the Google Brotli decompression library that can allow memory reading or corruption through a crafted Brotli stream.
  • The issue affects unpatched .NET 8, 9, 10, and pre-RC3 .NET 11 releases when applications decompress attacker-controlled Brotli data, while .NET Framework is not affected.
  • Microsoft released fixes in .NET 8.0.33, 9.0.22, 10.0.14, and 11 RC3 on 25 October 2026.
  • CISA added CVE-2026-111497 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 27 October 2026, with reported exploitation so far focused on Node.js.
  • Organizations should update affected runtimes and, until patching is complete, remove or block Brotli decompression for untrusted requests, HTTP responses, and application inputs.

Millions of security cameras at risk: DoS vulnerability in Intelbras devices — May Read

Intelbras patched an unauthenticated firmware-update endpoint in several Mibo IP camera models that let anyone on the local network repeatedly force cameras offline. Users should update to firmware R.260804 to mitigate the denial-of-service flaw.

  • Researchers identified an unauthenticated firmware-update endpoint in Intelbras IP camera firmware that could be used by someone on the local Wi-Fi network to force a camera offline.
  • The issue affected firmware v240927 on the Intelbras iM3B-C and, according to Intelbras, the same firmware was compatible with the iMX C, iM4 C, iM5 SC, iME 360 C, and iM7+ FC models.
  • Sending a firmware upload request triggered the camera reboot process even when the supplied firmware was not valid, and periodic requests could keep the device offline indefinitely.
  • Intelbras released firmware R.260804, which adds checks for authentication session and cookie data before allowing firmware updates through the affected endpoint.
  • MITRE assigned the issue candidate ID CAN-2026-2035970 and classified it as medium severity with a CVSS 4.0 score of 5.1, pending final CVE assignment.

item.title: INJ3CTOR3 FreePBX Implant Exfiltrates SIP Trunk Credentials
item.content:encoded:
Window: 28 Oct 03:00 → 28 Oct 07:00 UTC (4 hours)

From Hijacked PBX to Stolen Trunk: INJ3CTOR3’s Campaign Evolves — Should Read

INJ3CTOR3’s updated FreePBX malware now exfiltrates SIP trunk, AMI, database, and mail credentials every minute, allowing toll fraud even after an infected PBX is rebuilt. Organizations must isolate and fully eradicate persistence mechanisms before rotating all exposed credentials, especially SIP trunk secrets.

  • INJ3CTOR3’s updated FreePBX implant uploads 17 configuration files containing SIP trunk, AMI, database, and mail-relay credentials to two staging hosts every minute while the host remains infected.
  • Stolen SIP trunk credentials can allow the operator to register with a carrier and place calls from another machine, so disinfecting or rebuilding the PBX alone does not end the risk.
  • The September build uses staging hosts 45.95.147.178 and 160.119.69.4, with credential uploads sent to /hima_data/index.php on both hosts.
  • The campaign’s persistence includes cron jobs, cached scripts, shell-profile and boot triggers, backdoor accounts, webshell copies, and immutable file settings that can rebuild other components.
  • The article recommends isolating a suspected PBX, preserving evidence, removing persistence mechanisms before other components, and rotating exposed credentials only after the host is clean.

item.title: FBI Seizes Virtualine.net in Operation Omegaline Targeting Omegatech
item.content:encoded:
Window: 27 Oct 19:00 → 27 Oct 23:00 UTC (4 hours)

Omegatech Is Disrupted, and the Pressure on Bulletproof Hosting Keeps Building — Should Read

Law enforcement’s seizure of Virtualine/Omegatech reflects growing pressure on bulletproof hosting providers, but these operators can rapidly evade disruption by shifting IP ranges and customers to new ASNs and shell companies. Defenders should continuously track infrastructure patterns, newly populated ASNs, and sanctions-linked entities rather than relying on static blocklists.

  • The FBI seized virtualine.net on October 27, 2026, under Operation Omegaline, following an investigation led by the FBI Washington Field Office with law-enforcement partners in Germany, the Netherlands, and the United Kingdom.
  • Silent Push observed infrastructure moving from Railnet LLC (AS214943) to Omegatech (AS202412) in February 2026 and identified Virtualine Technologies within Omegatech’s network.
  • Omegatech was not fully offline after the seizure, but its network address ranges showed very low routing visibility, which the article says typically indicates a serious operator-side problem.
  • In 2026, authorities also seized more than 800 servers associated with THE.Hosting/WorkTitans BV and arrested two men, while the EU sanctioned Media Land, ML Cloud, and general director Aleksandr Volosovik.
  • The article states that bulletproof hosting providers can obtain a new network identifier within two to five business days and move the same malicious internet address ranges to it, making static blocklists quickly outdated.

Technologies: cloud-platform, network-monitoring

item.title: Yoba Malware Uses Signed ChatGPT and Claude Installers for DLL Sideloading
item.content:encoded:
Window: 27 Oct 11:00 → 27 Oct 15:00 UTC (4 hours)

An insecure neighbor: how a vulnerability chain led to an isolation bypass in cloud infrastructure — Should Read

A Kaspersky-led bug bounty assessment found that chained flaws in a major cloud provider’s managed Kubernetes and internal management infrastructure could let a normal tenant escape a worker node, compromise control-plane systems, and bypass isolation between tenants. The issues included insecure privileged pod controls, a Konnectivity SSRF-to-RCE path, flat overlay networking, exposed monitoring/logging data, and weaknesses in managed database and SaltStack services; the provider reportedly fixed the findings.

  • Researchers participating in an official bug bounty program found that a managed Kubernetes cluster allowed tenants to create privileged pods with host access, enabling root access to a worker node.
  • A Konnectivity service token found on the worker node could be used with a flaw in the Konnectivity server to make network connections from the Kubernetes control plane and ultimately execute commands there.
  • The provider’s shared overlay network exposed managed-service infrastructure, while VictoriaMetrics and VictoriaLogs endpoints revealed other tenants’ control-plane targets and logs containing root SSH private keys.
  • Researchers identified additional paths to compromise managed Kafka, Redis/Valkey, PostgreSQL, and MySQL services through exposed or improperly configured components, potentially allowing access to other tenants’ data or command execution on their hosts.
  • A vulnerable custom SaltStack script enabled SQL injection against the provider’s cloud-management database, exposing Salt master authentication tokens that could run commands on cloud minions; the provider was notified and fixed the reported issues.

Technologies: cloud-platform, container-platform, orchestration, database, message-queue, network-monitoring, object-storage, backup, operating-system

Products: k0s, kubernetes, konnectivity-server, saltstack, victoriametrics, victorialogs, apache-kafka, redis-exporter, patroni, etcd, valkey, mysql, ubuntu

Vendors: mirantis, kubernetes-project, victoriametrics, apache-software-foundation, valkey-project, oracle, zalando, salt-project

Tricks from the Past deployed via signed ChatGPT and Claude binaries — Should Read

Check Point Research uncovered the Yoba campaign, which uses fake GitHub pages for purported ChatGPT and Claude desktop apps to distribute malware through DLL sideloading of legitimate signed OpenAI and Anthropic executables. The malware persists via scheduled tasks and retrieves attacker-controlled payloads through Telegram-seeded DGA domains and DNS-over-HTTPS, with XMRig cryptomining observed as the final payload.

  • Check Point Research tracked a campaign called Yoba that used fake GitHub repositories and GitHub Pages promoting purported ChatGPT and Claude desktop applications, including GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-6 Astra, and Claude Opus.
  • The malicious installers packaged a DLL named winmm.dll alongside legitimate signed OpenAI or Anthropic Setup.exe files, allowing the malware to run through DLL sideloading.
  • YobaDropper creates a ProgramData\WMProcess directory, copies the legitimate Windows WMPDMC.exe program there, drops the YobaLoader as wmpdui.dll, and creates a scheduled task running as Local System for persistence.
  • YobaLoader uses a Telegram channel profile image to generate a domain, queries Google DNS-over-HTTPS for a signed and encrypted DNS TXT command, and can download a next-stage payload from Catbox.
  • Researchers observed the loader injecting an XMRig 6.26.0 cryptocurrency miner into svchost.exe, while noting that the loader can also deliver other PE or PowerShell payloads.

Technologies: operating-system, source-control

Products: chatgpt, claude, windows, github, github-pages, google-public-dns, telegram, tor, xmrig

Vendors: openai, anthropic, microsoft, github, google, telegram, catbox, tor-project

Introducing the Cloudflare PHP Capture the Flag challenge — Optional

Cloudflare launched a HackerOne-backed PHP Capture the Flag challenge inviting researchers to bypass its WAF, exploit PHP 8.5.11 vulnerabilities CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, and retrieve a sandboxed flag. Valid, materially distinct RCE-and-flag-recovery bypasses submitted under the program rules may qualify for a bounty.

  • Cloudflare launched a limited-time PHP Capture the Flag challenge through its HackerOne bug bounty program to test whether researchers can bypass its web application firewall protections.
  • The challenge targets CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 in stock PHP 8.5.11 running with Apache 2 via mod_php in a Cloudflare Container.
  • Participants must use an authorized POST request to achieve attacker-controlled PHP code or command execution, recover the current contents of /flag, and verify the flag through the challenge interface.
  • To claim a bounty, researchers must submit a private, complete, reproducible report to Cloudflare on HackerOne, and awards require a materially distinct bypass method or exploit payload.
  • Cloudflare states that its web application firewall can help protect exposed systems but is not a substitute for applying relevant PHP security updates.

Technologies: waf, container-platform, web-server, cloud-platform

Products: cloudflare-web-application-firewall, cloudflare-containers, php-8-5-11, apache-http-server

The Impact of AI on CVEs: INDUSTRY CHALLENGES — Optional

AI is rapidly increasing both legitimate and fabricated CVE reports, overwhelming maintainers and vulnerability databases while making accurate severity assessment and patch prioritization harder. Organizations need to validate real-world exposure rather than rely solely on volume or CVSS base scores.

  • Generative AI is increasing the volume of both legitimate vulnerability discoveries and low-quality or fabricated reports, creating verification burdens for maintainers and vulnerability databases.
  • The curl project ended its bug bounty program in January 2026 after AI-generated submissions contributed to a flood of invalid reports, with confirmed vulnerabilities representing less than 5% of submissions.
  • NIST changed NVD prioritization in April 2026 to focus on CISA’s Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog, federal software, and critical software, while moving older backlogged CVEs to “Not Scheduled.”
  • JFrog found that 54 of 55 advisories published by a newly created GitHub account, including reports targeting SQLite, were fabricated and contained nonexistent code references, impossible line numbers, or unsupported fix claims.
  • AI-assisted discovery is increasing remediation queues, while organizations still need to verify reports, identify affected systems, test fixes, and deploy updates.

Technologies: database

Whole-of-state defense: How SLED agencies can secure critical infrastructure in the AI era — Optional

AI is expanding the cyberattack surface for state, local, and education organizations that operate critical infrastructure, making under-resourced utilities, schools, and local governments attractive entry points. The article advocates a whole-of-state model with shared visibility, governance, services, and prioritized management of IT, OT, identity, cloud, and AI exposures.

  • SLED organizations operate critical infrastructure including water treatment plants, transportation systems, public hospitals, schools, and emergency communications, and nearly 90% of state CIOs rate cyberattacks on critical systems as a high concern.
  • AI expands SLED cyber risk because employees can build unapproved AI-enabled applications, vendors add AI features and connectors that can expand data access, and attackers use automation to conduct reconnaissance faster.
  • Federal agencies warned in July that cyber threat actors were targeting internet-connected operational technology in the water and wastewater sector, including programmable logic controllers whose passwords and IP addresses were altered to lock out operators.
  • A whole-of-state approach treats state agencies, local governments, schools, and utilities as one defensive perimeter through shared governance, visibility of assets and security findings, and cybersecurity services.
  • The article recommends maintaining an inventory of critical assets and AI tools, prioritizing exposures by exploitability and public-safety impact, sharing visibility across jurisdictions, and establishing policies for AI use.

Products: tenable-one, tenable-one-ot-exposure

Identifying AI agents: Bringing visibility and control to Castle — Optional

Castle has introduced AI-agent identification that uses Web Bot Auth, browser fingerprinting, network signals, and user-agent strings to identify agents such as ChatGPT agent and Perplexity Comet. The company emphasizes that cryptographic authentication offers stronger identity assurance than fingerprinting or user-agent detection, while agent identification remains distinct from bot and abuse detection.

  • Castle has added AI-agent identification that associates identified agent identities with application events and exposes the information through its API.
  • Castle identifies agents using cryptographic Web Bot Auth where available, as well as browser fingerprinting, network-level information, and user-agent strings.
  • Web Bot Auth verifies that requests were signed by a key associated with a known agent operator, while fingerprinting and user-agent strings do not provide the same authentication guarantee.
  • Castle distinguishes AI agents, AI browsers, and browser automation, including agents such as Meta Muse, OpenAI Dots, Grok Bot, ChatGPT agent, and Instinct, plus Perplexity Comet.
  • Castle states that AI-agent identification, bot detection, and abuse detection are complementary because automated AI-agent traffic is not necessarily malicious.

Brotli2Shell: Frequently asked questions for Google Brotli decoder vulnerability (CVE-2026-111497) — Must Read

CVE-2026-111497 (Brotli2Shell) is a critical out-of-bounds write in the Google Brotli decoder that can enable remote code execution when applications decompress attacker-controlled data. Organizations should update affected Brotli-dependent software, including Node.js, .NET, Bun, Envoy, Istio, Python packages, and PHP Windows builds, then restart or redeploy affected workloads.

  • CVE-2026-111497, also called Brotli2Shell, is an out-of-bounds write flaw in Google’s Brotli decoder that Google scored 9.2 under CVSSv4.0.
  • An attacker can trigger the flaw by causing an application to unpack crafted Brotli data, including through compressed HTTP responses or compressed request bodies.
  • Affected software includes Google Brotli, Node.js, Bun, Envoy Proxy, Istio, supported Microsoft .NET releases, Python Brotli packages, and PHP Windows builds, with fixed versions listed in the article.
  • The possible effects range from a program crash and memory disclosure to potential remote code execution, and public proof-of-concept code is available.
  • Organizations should install fixed application releases and restart or redeploy affected processes, containers, and scheduled jobs because updating only a system Brotli library does not fix software that includes its own copy.

Malicious Firefox Extensions Impersonate Phantom, Jupiter, and Bitget to Steal Wallet Secrets — Should Read

Malicious Firefox extensions impersonating Phantom, Jupiter, and Bitget wallets used copied branding and Unicode lookalike names to steal recovery phrases and private keys, sending them to bonto.io-controlled servers. Anyone who installed one and entered wallet secrets should treat the wallet as compromised and immediately move funds to a newly created wallet on a clean device.

  • Socket’s Threat Research Team identified malicious Firefox extensions impersonating Phantom, Jupiter, and Bitget that steal wallet recovery phrases and private keys.
  • The extensions used Unicode lookalike characters, copied branding, and separate throwaway Firefox Add-ons developer accounts to make their listings appear legitimate.
  • The Phantom impersonator included a loader that fetched code from phantom.bonto.io/config and ran it in every page a victim opened, while also containing a bundled stealer.
  • The Jupiter and Bitget impersonators contained built-in stealers that sent captured wallet secrets to jupiter.bonto.io and bitget.bonto.io.
  • The three confirmed listings were removed from Firefox Add-ons as of publication, but users who entered secrets into them are advised to treat their wallets as compromised and move funds to a new wallet.

Technologies: browser, cloud-platform

Tricks from the Past deployed via signed ChatGPT and Claude binaries — Should Read

Check Point Research uncovered the Yoba campaign, which uses fake GitHub pages for purported ChatGPT and Claude desktop apps and DLL sideloading through legitimate signed OpenAI and Anthropic executables to install malware. The chain persists via scheduled tasks and uses Telegram-seeded DGA domains, Google DNS-over-HTTPS, and signed encrypted tasking to deliver payloads, including an XMRig cryptominer over Tor.

  • Check Point Research tracked the Yoba campaign, which used fake GitHub repositories and GitHub Pages promoting purported desktop applications named GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-6 Astra, and Claude Opus.
  • The malicious ZIP packages included legitimate signed OpenAI or Anthropic Setup.exe files that loaded a malicious winmm.dll file, a method known as DLL sideloading.
  • YobaDropper checks for administrator privileges, creates a ProgramData\WMProcess directory, copies the legitimate Windows WMPDMC.exe there, and uses a scheduled task running as Local System to load its next-stage wmpdui.dll file.
  • YobaLoader obtains tasking through a Telegram channel profile image, generates a dedyn.io domain, queries Google DNS-over-HTTPS for a TXT record, verifies an Ed25519 signature, and retrieves a payload from Catbox.
  • The observed final payload was XMRig 6.26.0, configured to mine through a Tor proxy, although the loader can deliver PE files or PowerShell scripts.

An insecure neighbor: how a vulnerability chain led to an isolation bypass in cloud infrastructure — Should Read

Researchers chained multiple flaws in a major cloud provider’s managed Kubernetes and shared overlay infrastructure to bypass tenant isolation and potentially take over other customers’ clusters, databases, storage, and cloud management systems. The case highlights that provider-side misconfigurations, exposed management interfaces, leaked credentials, and weak network segmentation can create cloud-wide compromise paths.

  • The cloud provider’s managed Kubernetes service allowed a regular tenant to create a privileged pod with host access, giving root access to a worker node.
  • A Konnectivity design flaw let a compromised worker node request network connections from the Kubernetes control plane, which researchers used to execute code on the control-plane host before escalating privileges.
  • The provider’s flat shared overlay network exposed management and monitoring services, allowing access to other tenants’ cluster metadata, logs containing root SSH keys, and potentially their managed resources.
  • Unauthenticated or improperly exposed services in the overlay network enabled paths to compromise managed Kafka, Redis or Valkey, PostgreSQL, and MySQL instances belonging to other customers.
  • A SQL injection in a custom SaltStack component exposed Salt master authentication tokens, which could be used to run commands on cloud minions; the researchers reported the issues through the provider’s bug bounty program and stated they were fully fixed.

Technologies: cloud-platform, container-platform, orchestration, database, network-monitoring, message-queue, object-storage, backup

Omegatech Is Disrupted, and the Pressure on Bulletproof Hosting Keeps Building — Should Read

Law enforcement’s seizure of Virtualine/Omegatech reflects growing pressure on bulletproof hosting providers, but these operators can rapidly evade disruption by shifting IP ranges and customers to new ASNs and shell companies. Defenders should continuously track infrastructure patterns, newly populated ASNs, and sanctions-linked entities rather than relying on static blocklists.

  • The FBI seized virtualine.net on October 27, 2026, under Operation Omegaline, following an investigation led by the FBI Washington Field Office with law-enforcement partners in Germany, the Netherlands, and the United Kingdom.
  • Silent Push observed infrastructure moving from Railnet LLC (AS214943) to Omegatech (AS202412) in February 2026 and identified Virtualine Technologies within Omegatech’s network.
  • Omegatech was not fully offline after the seizure, but its network address ranges showed very low routing visibility, which the article says typically indicates a serious operator-side problem.
  • In 2026, authorities also seized more than 800 servers associated with THE.Hosting/WorkTitans BV and arrested two men, while the EU sanctioned Media Land, ML Cloud, and general director Aleksandr Volosovik.
  • The article states that bulletproof hosting providers can obtain a new network identifier within two to five business days and move the same malicious internet address ranges to it, making static blocklists quickly outdated.

The Enclosed Document Was the Supplier's Logo — May Read

A compromised supplier Microsoft 365 mailbox sent a convincing BCC phishing email whose only attachment was a harmless signature logo, while directing recipients to manually type an attacker-controlled hostname. The incident shows why email defenses must detect inconsistencies between message claims, sender behavior, and plain-text lures rather than relying only on authentication and attachment scanning.

  • A UK plant and tool hire company received a BCC email from a small agricultural supplier's genuine Microsoft 365 mailbox, with the sender listed in the To field and recipients hidden on BCC.
  • The message claimed to contain documents, but its only recorded attachment was a 27,804-byte JPEG matching the supplier's inline signature logo and it scanned clean.
  • The email instructed recipients to copy and paste a plain-text hostname with no hyperlink, leaving the incident's links array, QR fields, and OCR fields empty.
  • The sender passed SPF, DKIM, and DMARC at origin, while final-hop authentication failures were attributed to inbound gateway processing that modified the message body.
  • A depot hire desk user reported the email because the supposed document message pointed to an unrelated domain, after which an analyst classified it as malicious and quarantined both recipient mailboxes.

The Impact of AI on CVEs: INDUSTRY CHALLENGES — Optional

AI is accelerating both genuine vulnerability discovery and a flood of fabricated or overstated CVE reports, overwhelming maintainers, scoring systems, and enterprise remediation teams. Organizations need stronger verification and risk-based prioritization rather than relying solely on CVSS severity or raw CVE volume.

  • Generative AI has increased both the speed of legitimate vulnerability discovery and the volume of low-quality or fabricated vulnerability reports.
  • curl ended its bug bounty program in January 2026 after AI-generated submissions contributed to invalid reports and fewer than 5% of submissions were confirmed as vulnerabilities.
  • NIST changed National Vulnerability Database prioritization in April 2026, focusing on known exploited issues, U.S. federal software, and critical software while placing older backlogged records into a "Not Scheduled" status.
  • JFrog reported that 54 of 55 advisories published by a newly created GitHub account, including advisories targeting SQLite, were fabricated and contained references to nonexistent code, impossible line numbers, or nonexistent fixes.
  • The article states that AI-assisted discovery is increasing remediation queues faster than maintainers can verify, fix, test, and release patches.

Censys AI Agents: Automate Investigations and Amplify Your Threat Intel — Optional

Censys has launched an API for its Investigator agentic framework, enabling scripts, SOAR playbooks, and AI agents to expand known indicators into related infrastructure, detection artifacts, and monitorable CenQL queries. The service is positioned for automated CTI enrichment, SOC triage, and incident response scoping.

  • Censys Investigator now has an API that accepts domains, IP addresses, and full threat-intelligence reports from scripts, SOAR playbooks, and AI agents.
  • Each investigation returns a downloadable report of related infrastructure, including IPs, domains, services sharing fingerprints, and a CenQL query intended to match the identified cluster.
  • Censys describes use cases for the API in threat-intelligence enrichment, escalated SOC alert triage, and digital forensics and incident response.
  • In an example based on a Microsoft phishing report, Censys Investigator expanded seven listed domains into a 69-asset cluster and identified additional domains not included in Microsoft’s list.
  • Investigations do not consume Censys Credits, but each user may run three concurrently, organizations are limited to 150 per week, and results are retained for seven days.

Whole-of-state defense: How SLED agencies can secure critical infrastructure in the AI era — Optional

AI is expanding the cyberattack surface for state, local, and education organizations that operate critical infrastructure, making under-resourced utilities, schools, and local governments attractive entry points. The article advocates a whole-of-state model with shared visibility, governance, services, and prioritized management of IT, OT, identity, cloud, and AI exposures.

  • SLED organizations operate critical infrastructure including water treatment plants, transportation systems, public hospitals, schools, and emergency communications, and nearly 90% of state CIOs rate cyberattacks on critical systems as a high concern.
  • AI expands SLED cyber risk because employees can build unapproved AI-enabled applications, vendors add AI features and connectors that can expand data access, and attackers use automation to conduct reconnaissance faster.
  • Federal agencies warned in July that cyber threat actors were targeting internet-connected operational technology in the water and wastewater sector, including programmable logic controllers whose passwords and IP addresses were altered to lock out operators.
  • A whole-of-state approach treats state agencies, local governments, schools, and utilities as one defensive perimeter through shared governance, visibility of assets and security findings, and cybersecurity services.
  • The article recommends maintaining an inventory of critical assets and AI tools, prioritizing exposures by exploitability and public-safety impact, sharing visibility across jurisdictions, and establishing policies for AI use.

Introducing the Cloudflare PHP Capture the Flag challenge — Optional

Cloudflare launched a HackerOne CTF inviting researchers to bypass its WAF protections for the php2shell PHP flaws, achieve RCE in a deliberately vulnerable PHP sandbox, and retrieve a flag. The challenge is limited to authorized POST testing on designated endpoints and rewards materially distinct, reproducible bypasses.

  • Cloudflare launched a limited-time PHP Capture the Flag challenge through its HackerOne bug bounty program to test whether researchers can bypass its web application firewall protections.
  • The challenge targets CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, the PHP vulnerabilities referred to as php2shell.
  • The target uses stock PHP 8.5.11 with Apache 2 via mod_php, an empty index.php, and a /flag file inside a Cloudflare Container.
  • To qualify for a bounty, participants must demonstrate attacker-controlled code or command execution, recover and verify the current /flag contents, and submit a complete private HackerOne report.
  • Cloudflare states that its WAF can help protect exposed systems but is not a substitute for applying the relevant PHP security updates.

Identifying AI agents: Bringing visibility and control to Castle — Optional

Castle has introduced AI-agent identification that uses cryptographic Web Bot Auth, fingerprinting, network signals, and user-agent detection to help organizations identify and apply policies to agents such as ChatGPT, Grok, and Perplexity Comet. The company emphasizes that agent identity is distinct from bot and abuse detection, and that only cryptographic authentication provides strong assurance of an agent's claimed identity.

  • Castle introduced AI agent identification that labels events from AI agents, AI browsers, and browser automation tools with the agent’s name, operator, category, and identification method.
  • Castle uses Web Bot Auth to verify cryptographically signed requests, while fingerprinting, network information, and user-agent strings provide weaker ways to recognize agents.
  • The article states that authenticating an agent establishes the identity of the signer but does not determine whether the agent’s activity is safe or should be allowed.
  • Organizations can use agent identification to investigate activity, measure agent adoption, and apply different requirements to sensitive actions such as payments or account changes.
  • Castle distinguishes AI agent identification from bot and abuse detection, noting that automated traffic may have a high bot score without necessarily being malicious.

Silent Push has integrated its Threat Check and infrastructure-enrichment capabilities into Abstract Security, allowing joint customers to automatically identify and alert on verified adversary-owned domains and IPs directly in their data pipelines.

Brotli2Shell: Frequently asked questions for Google Brotli decoder vulnerability (CVE-2026-111497) — Must Read

CVE-2026-111497 (Brotli2Shell) is a critical out-of-bounds write in the Google Brotli decoder that can enable remote code execution when applications decompress attacker-controlled data. Organizations should update affected Brotli-dependent software, including Node.js, .NET, Bun, Envoy, Istio, Python packages, and PHP Windows builds, then restart or redeploy affected workloads.

  • CVE-2026-111497, also called Brotli2Shell, is an out-of-bounds write flaw in Google’s Brotli decoder that Google scored 9.2 under CVSSv4.0.
  • An attacker can trigger the flaw by causing an application to unpack crafted Brotli data, including through compressed HTTP responses or compressed request bodies.
  • Affected software includes Google Brotli, Node.js, Bun, Envoy Proxy, Istio, supported Microsoft .NET releases, Python Brotli packages, and PHP Windows builds, with fixed versions listed in the article.
  • The possible effects range from a program crash and memory disclosure to potential remote code execution, and public proof-of-concept code is available.
  • Organizations should install fixed application releases and restart or redeploy affected processes, containers, and scheduled jobs because updating only a system Brotli library does not fix software that includes its own copy.

Technologies: proxy, orchestration
